newsitem.title: USA: Bank NY sees State Street stake passive.
newsitem.headline: Bank NY sees State Street stake passive.

text.p: Bank of New York Co Inc Chairman and Chief Executive J. Carter Bacot reiterated in an interview on Tuesday that the company's investment in State Street Corp is passive.
"All we've said is, we want to have a passive investment," Bacot said in an interview prior to Bank of New York's annual meeting of shareholders.

Bank of New York owns 4.9 percent of State Street and wants to raise the stake to 9.99 percent. Bacot said Bank of New York is in court challenging a ruling by the Massachusetts Board of Bank Incorporation that is keeping Bank of New York from raising its stake. Bacot said Bank of New York believe the Massachusetts action is an unconstitutional restraint on interstate commerce.
Asked what the strategy was behind the investment, Bacot said, "We have done well with the original investment. We'd just like to have more of a good thing."

Bacot said Bank of New York continues to be interested in acquiring securities processing and custody businesses. "The business is consolidating in all of its phases," he said. "As long as there are willing sellers, we will be an active buyer."
Asked how business was going at the midpoint of the second quarter, he said it was "on target," and added, "We're pleased so far."
He declined to comment on First Call consensus earnings estimates of $2.75 per share this year and $0.67 per share for the second quarter, saying they were "ballpark figures."
Bacot said Bank of New York is taking a "neutral" stance on the credit-card business, and hopes that the charge-off rate will peak in the second half of 1997.

Bacot said he believes that the trend toward consolidation in the financial services industry will continue and he believes eventually there will be "a level playing field" in which anybody can acquire anybody else, even if they are in a different segment of the business.
"It's just a matter of time," he said.
